text: A savings account is a deposit account that allows customers to store money and earn interest. Banks may apply minimum balance requirements and account-specific fees. Interest rates and fees depend on the account terms.
A fixed deposit is an investment where a customer deposits a lump sum for a fixed period at an agreed interest rate. Premature withdrawal may attract a penalty depending on the bank's terms.
A personal loan is an unsecured loan offered to an eligible borrower. Approval and interest rates depend on factors such as income, credit history, repayment capacity, and lender policy.
A credit card allows a cardholder to make purchases using a credit limit. The cardholder must repay the amount by the due date. Interest and late payment charges may apply to unpaid balances.
Know Your Customer (KYC) is a process banks use to verify customer identity. It may require identity and address documents. Requirements vary by jurisdiction and institution.
NEFT is an electronic funds transfer system used to transfer money between bank accounts. Transfer processing and limits are governed by the applicable bank and payment-system rules.
IMPS is an electronic funds transfer service that supports near real-time interbank transfers. Availability, transaction limits, and charges depend on the bank and applicable rules.
